::: {.proj-layout}
::: {.proj-main}
::: {.question-card}
## Research question

How do electrolyzers, hydrogen storage and fuel cells change the cost, curtailment and firm output of a grid-connected wind farm?
:::

::: {.proj-cards}
::: {.info-card .glow-card .ic-contribution}
## My contribution

First author. Extended NREL's REopt optimization model with hydrogen components and ran the analysis.
:::

::: {.info-card .glow-card .ic-method}
## Method

Mixed-integer sizing and dispatch optimization for a 253-MW West Texas wind farm with ERCOT prices, with sensitivities to hydrogen price, region and future technology costs.
:::

:::

## Key findings

::: {.findings}
1. In the Journal of Mechanical Design case study, adding an electrolyzer reduced total system cost by about 7%.
2. In the same study, using hydrogen storage with fuel cells reduced it by about 26% and sharply cut curtailment (the earlier TORQUE 2022 case reported about 9% and 30%).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Boundary conditions"}
Cost assumptions date from 2020–2023 and predate final federal hydrogen credit rules.
:::

:::
